docs.text:
RGHC entered into a Shareholders’ Agreement on May 5, 2026, for the formation of Clark World Trade Center, Inc.

On April 30, 2026, the Board of Directors approved a 20% equity stake in Clark World Trade Center, Inc. This investment is valued at PHP 240M.

This transaction is a significant step toward accelerating growth and fostering innovation through strategic partnerships. The investment offers strong potential for financial returns and improves risk management by diversifying our portfolio against market fluctuations.Strategically, this initiative enhances RGHC’s presence in a key Philippine economic zone and global trade gateway. By establishing a foothold in this rapidly growing commercial hub, RGHC is well-positioned to sustain long-term competitiveness and play an active role in the region's future development.

Under the shareholders’ agreement, RGHC will subscribe to 2.4M shares at a Par Value of P100.00 per share for PHP 240M, representing 20% stake of CWTCI.

RGHC and the shareholders have agreed to incorporate CWTCI with the Securities and Exchange Commission in accordance with Philippine Law. As a new entity, CWTCI will develop, own, and operate the Clark World Trade Center Exhibition and Convention Venue (the "Project"), envisioned as the premier venue within the Clark Freeport Zone in Pampanga. To facilitate this, Clark WTC Development Corporation, the primary lessee for approximately 60 hectares of land from Clark International Airport Corporation will sublease a portion of this land to CWTCI for the construction and operation of the Project.The complex will be managed by World Trade Center Management, Inc., which holds the exclusive license from the World Trade Centers Association to operate the World Trade Center brand in the Philippines.

Two hundred forty million pesos (Php 240,000,000.00)

The total consideration is set at par value, to be paid in four installments.

- First Installment (25%): Due within 5 business days after Shareholders receive notice that CWDC has been awarded the master lease.- Second Installment (25%): Due within 90 days after the First Installment is paid or upon CWTCI receiving its SEC Certificate of Incorporation, whichever occurs earlier.- Third Installment (25%): Due within 90 days after the Second Installment.- Fourth Installment (25%): Due within 90 days after the Third Installment.

Please be advised that RGHC entered into an Investment Agreement on May 6, 2026, regarding the incorporation of SPPI Aero-Logistics Park, Inc. (SAPI).This agreement replaces the Joint Venture Agreement previously disclosed on May 4, 2026.

On April 30, 2026, the Board of Directors approved a 10% stake in SPPI Aero-Logistics Park, Inc. This investment is valued at PHP 48M.

Republic Glass Holdings Corporation views the aero-logistic park as a timely and promising business opportunity. The initiative supports our goal of building strong strategic partnerships while offering solid potential for financial returns. Furthermore, it enhances our risk management by diversifying our investment portfolio and reducing exposure to market fluctuations.The project’s location provides a significant advantage. Its proximity to Clark International Airport will streamline the movement of goods and improve access to both domestic and international markets.Strategically, this development strengthens our presence in one of the Philippines’ key economic zones. It positions RGHC to benefit from the continued growth of this rapidly expanding commercial hub.

Under the Investment Agreement, RGHC will subscribe to 480K shares at a Par Value of P100.00 per share for PHP 48M, representing10% stake of SAPI.

RGHC and the investors have agreed to incorporate SAPI with the Securities and Exchange Commission in accordance with Philippine law. SPPI Aero-Logistics Park, Inc (SAPI) will develop and operate a logistics and industrial park adjacent to Clark International Airport. Clark WTC Development Corp. (CWDC) will enter into a long-term lease agreement with Clark International Airport Corporation (CIAC). Subsequently, CWDC will sublease the land to SAPI with CIAC's conformity, establishing SAPI as the sub-lessee for the project.

Forty-eight million pesos (Php 48,000,000.00)

The total consideration is set at Php100 per share, multiplied by the total number of shares subscribed.

Payment will be made in two installments:- First Installment (10%): Due upon filing the application for the incorporation of the SAPI with the SEC.- Second Installment (90%): Due within 90 days of the first installment payment or upon SAPI receiving its SEC Certificate of Incorporation, whichever occurs earlier.
